question: What happens to an enemy who sees the tilaka?
premises: The verse says someone makes a tilaka.
It says an enemy sees him.
It says the enemy is fivefold.
inference: An enemy who sees the tilaka becomes fivefold, that is, multiplied or overpowered.
uncertainties: pañcadhā may mean fivefold in a ritual sense.
plain_english: Whoever makes the tilaka, an enemy who sees him becomes fivefold.
